title: The identity gene Fezf2 is repurposed postnatally to specify inhibitory input in an activity-dependent manner
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02515-6Kroon et al. show that Fezf2, the gene that gives a cortical neuron its identity before birth, is reused postnatally under the control of neuronal activity to set how much inhibition that neuron receives.

title: Highly selective visual circuits in mouse frontal cortex
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02520-9The authors identify neurons in the frontal cortex of awake mice with highly selective visual receptive fields. These neurons prioritize encoding of binocular visual space, require V1 input and provide functional feedback throughout the visual cortex.

title: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02523-6Using fMRI data from speakers of 21 languages and multilingual language models, de Varda et al. show that brain encoding models trained on some languages predict responses to unseen languages, pointing to a shared meaning component across languages.

title: Presynaptic functional organization by phase separation

title: Brain Predicts Spoken Mandarin Differently Than English
summary: Most neuroscience models of how we predict upcoming speech are based on English and European languages.
